While stationed in Kotzebue, he met and married Carrie Williams. Carrie Williams Qisiliaq Uhl was born in 1922 in Kotzebue, Alaska. For most of her lifetime she lived in the country, away from town and any public services such as running water or electricity. Her family led a very subsistence-based lifestyle which meant that they depended on hunting, fishing, and gathering to provide food for themselves and their extended family. For over five decades, Bob and Carrie Uhl lived in rural camps. Some of the major activities occurring within the district include: livestock grazing, wildland fire suppression, as well as motorized and non-motorized recreation. The Boise District is divided into three geographic areas/field offices: Bruneau (1.4 million acres), Four Rivers (1.3 million acres) and Owyhee (1.2 million acres). The District also manages Idaho's only National Conservation Area, Morley Nelson Snake River Birds of Prey (487,000 acres), home to the greatest concentration of nesting birds of prey in North America – and perhaps, the world. Some 800 pairs of hawks, owls, eagles and falcons come each spring to mate and raise their young here. pages.text: Bomba and bioluminescence—Puerto Rico is full of surprises | National Geographic By Amanda Canning Last updated December 17, 2025 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). The inhabitants of San Juan aren’t early risers. At 9am, the city’s streets are largely empty. In the Plaza Colón, there’s a cockerel scrabbling about in the flower beds. A kiosk selling coffee and empanadas is untroubled by customers. “We like a slow start,” Laura Ortiz-Villamil confirms as we sit in the shade, the sun already blazing. In front of us is a statue of Christopher Columbus, a crucifix raised in his left hand. Among the first Europeans to barrel over the Atlantic, all eager to get their hands on whatever land they could, he ‘discovered’ Puerto Rico in 1493 and immediately claimed it for Spain. “The Spanish called it Puerto Rico — rich port — wrongly believing there was gold here,” Laura says as we set off on a stroll around the capital’s historic district, Old San Juan. A born-and-bred Puerto Rican, with tattoos on her arms ranging from Gabriel García Márquez quotes to Peanuts characters, historian Laura set up her guiding company in 2022 to share her country’s “less-known stories, good or bad”. We wander cobbled streets flanked by houses with arched wooden doorways and overhanging balconies, painted in every colour you might think of: pistachio, peach, lemon, spearmint. Some are in a state of beautiful decay, untouched for centuries; others are as spick and span as if the decorators only just moved out. Close booktiger's Diary [转载]可不能“随手一标”！ Posted by booktiger on 17 October 2026 in Chinese (China) (‪中文(中国大陆)‬) . 可不能“随手一标”！ 来源：国家安全部 2026年10月17日07:03 北京 https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/Xri2QFc-6VPpZ6QLBaqjgw 一张看似普通的网络地图，一个出于“兴趣”的随手标注，竟可能危害国家秘密安全。近年来，随着地理信息技术的普及，“开放地图”平台逐渐走入公众视野，但其背后隐藏的国家安全风险却不容忽视。 一个“爱好”带来的麻烦 2021年，许某在社交媒体上被一张带有艺术风格的路网地图所吸引。出于好奇，他开始接触境外开放地图平台，并违法“翻墙”访问。许某凭借对居住地周边环境的了解，以及从互联网搜集的公开信息，开始在境外开放地图平台上标注各类地理信息，多次标注军队等涉密敏感单位的位置信息。国家安全机关发现许某违法行为后迅速采取行动，依法对其开展审查。面对审查，许某懊悔道：“我完全没想到，自己只是出于爱好做点标记，竟会触犯法律，威胁国家安全。”国家安全机关向其宣讲了相关法律法规，讲明了其行为的危害性，并依法对其进行处理。许某表示已深刻认识到错误，并积极配合消除隐患。 随手一标，隐患巨大 “开放地图”一般指数据开源、可自由使用与编辑的地图项目，经常由全球志愿者共同创建、编辑并免费共享地理数据，在碳中和、城乡交通建设、灾害风险评估研究等方面具备相应应用价值。但如果在开放地图平台上标注我国涉密敏感地理信息，就有可能被不法分子利用，对我国家安全造成危害。不法分子无需动用复杂的技术手段，仅凭开放地图便能轻易获取我国涉密敏感单位的位置、规模等信息，并据此在军事基地等涉密敏感单位附近开展“黑飞”、偷拍、测绘等活动。境外间谍情报机关还可能结合其他渠道获取的信息进行多源数据交叉比对，拼凑成完整情报，甚至还可能对涉密单位工作人员以及周边居民、商户等人员开展针对性的渗透、拉拢和策反活动，对我国家安全构成严重威胁。 国家安全机关提示 《 中华人民共和国保守国家秘密法 》《 中华人民共和国测绘法 》《 公开地图内容表示规范 》等法律法规划出清晰底线：个人或者组织非法获取、持有、提供、利用属于国家秘密的地理信息的，将被依法追责。开放地图不是个人兴趣的“涂鸦板”，看似无心的标注可能触碰国家秘密“红线”。 ——绷紧“安全弦”。增强国家安全意识，不在地图平台标注任何涉及军事基地、涉密单位的地理信息。 ——把好“出口关”。不在社交平台发布涉密场所周边照片、视频，拍照前留意背景是否涉及敏感场所，不转发、不扩散任何标注有涉密地理信息的地图内容。 ——当好“守护者”。如发现在公开地图标注涉密地理信息等危害国家安全的可疑情况，请及时通过12339国家安全机关举报受理电话、网络举报受理平台（ www.12339.gov.cn ）、国家安全部微信公众号举报受理渠道或者直接向当地国家安全机关进行举报。 Discussion Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

The 41-year-old Venezuelan was detained on Sunday when US Border Force and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers arrested him at El Paso International Airport. "On October 26, 2023, he entered the country with permission to stay for a temporary period, but in defiance of our nation's laws, he overstayed his welcome. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Br-12 Watchable Wildlife | Montana View Map In Full Screen This 200-acre prairie marsh in north central Montana holds a narrow reservoir about one mile long. This reservoir acts as a prairie pothole with its tailwaters slowly drying during the summer and fall. This water cycle permits waterfowl to hatch and raise young in this relatively isolated, resource-rich area, then move fledglings to major waters like the Missouri River. BR-12 also provides habitat for migrating waterfowl, upland birds, and upland wildlife species, so it’s not uncommon to observe 20-30 species in one spring day. Canvasback and redhead ducks regularly nest in the tailwaters, pelicans and tundra swans stop by for a rest and snack on their journeys, and even black terns (a species of concern) and loons have been observed utilizing BR-12’s “waterfowl facilities.” The area around BR-12 is short-grass prairie habitat. Species you might see associated with this habitat include chestnut-collared and McCowan’s longspur, horned lark, northern harrier, ferruginous hawk, Swainson’s hawk, burrowing owl, pronghorn, coyote, red fox, ground squirrel, and badger. The Constitution of the United States divides the federal government into three branches: Legislative Judicial Executive This ensures that no individual or group will have too much power. Legislative branch The legislative branch is made up of Congress : The U.S. Senate The U.S. House of Representatives It also includes special agencies and offices that provide support services to Congress. The legislative branch’s key roles include: Drafting proposed laws Confirming or rejecting presidential nominations for heads of federal agencies, federal judges, and the Supreme Court Surveying the budget Having the authority to declare war Judicial branch The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts. It evaluates laws by: Interpreting the meaning of laws Applying laws to individual cases Deciding if laws violate the Constitution Executive branch The president, the vice president, and the president's cabinet are the members of the executive branch. The executive branch’s key roles include: The president is the head of state, leader of the executive branch, and commander in chief of the United States armed forces. Close BrandonSimons_Aloe's Diary Mapping the Southern African grid from OpenStreetMap, and where the gaps are Posted by BrandonSimons_Aloe on 17 November 2026 in English . I run Aloe Energy, a small not-for-profit initiative working on energy access in Sub-Saharan Africa. We published a free interactive map of the Southern African Power Pool grid, and OpenStreetMap is its backbone, so I wanted to share how it was built and where OSM could use help. What we did. We took every OSM power line of 66 kV and above across the 12 SAPP countries (country extracts from November 2026). Where OSM had no line but an older public map did, we filled the gap from TANESCO (2015) and World Bank (2017) grid maps, but only for lines recorded as existing, with a known voltage, and more than about 3 km from any OSM line. A “Source and age” view on the map colors each line by where it comes from, so you can see exactly what is OSM and what is gap-fill. Where OSM is thin. Coverage is weakest in Tanzania, DR Congo and Angola. Those are the places where the map still leans on maps that are close to ten years old, and where new mapping would change the picture most. Substations named in national plans are often missing too. The map: https://aloeenergy.org/research/sapp-grid . Photograph by Markus Mauthe, laif/Redux TRAVEL Brazil's Best Kept Secret: The Pantanal The Amazon rain forest may get all the attention, but when it comes to wildlife, South America's biggest biodiversity star is the Pantanal. By Avery Stonich Published June 7, 2016 • 6 min read I get my first hint of the Pantanal 's impressive biodiversity as soon as I get off the plane in Corumbá , Brazil. White splotches cover the tarmac like some sort of Rorschach test on steroids. Bird droppings, I come to realize. The tropical heat drapes over me like a wool blanket; the thick air carries the raw scents of nature, a mix of earthy and sour. Part national park, part UNESCO World Heritage site , the Pantanal is the world’s largest tropical wetland, covering over 70,000 square miles—an area the size of Washington State—in the smack-dab center of South America. Brazil can lay claim to most of the region, but, as nature recognizes no political boundaries, the Pantanal spills into neighboring Paraguay and Bolivia. And though it's often overshadowed by the Amazon rain forest to the north, the Pantanal quietly boasts the highest concentration of wildlife on the continent . Life in the Pantanal follows the ebb and flow of an epic ecosystem that pulses with the seasons like a beating heart. Like many adolescents in her community, she struggled with pressures she felt unable to explain. She believed she simply had to endure them, and that having mental health problems meant someone was "crazy". Asking for help never seemed like an option. Today, her story is different. “I learned that I should not simply be scared,” Amina says. “I need to speak out. For Amina, learning about mental health did more than change her understanding. It gave her the confidence to seek support, and the reassurance that someone would listen. pages.text: Brian Mann : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Brian Mann Enlarge this image Nancie Battaglia/NPR Nancie Battaglia/NPR Brian Mann Correspondent, National Desk Brian Mann is NPR's first national addiction correspondent. He also covers breaking news in the U.S. and around the world. Mann began covering drug policy and the opioid crisis as part of a partnership between NPR and North Country Public Radio in New York. After joining NPR full time in 2020, Mann was one of the first national journalists to track the deadly spread of the synthetic opioid fentanyl, reporting from California and Washington state to West Virginia. After losing his father and stepbrother to substance abuse, Mann's reporting breaks down the stigma surrounding addiction and creates a factual basis for the ongoing national discussion. Mann has also served on NPR teams covering the Beijing Winter Olympics and the war in Ukraine. During a career in public radio that began in the 1980s, Mann has won numerous regional and national Edward R. Murrow awards. He is author of a 2006 book about small town politics called Welcome to the Homeland , described by T he Atlantic as "one of the best books to date on the putative-red-blue divide." Mann grew up in Alaska and is now based in New York's Adirondack Mountains. His audio postcards, broadcast on NPR, describe his backcountry trips into wild places around the world. This raucous, torch-lit parade in Lewes features brass bands, bagpipes and firecrackers as well as a procession of giant, caricature effigies. Photograph by Sussex News; Alamy By Orla Thomas Last updated November 1, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). ‘Remember, remember, the fifth of November’, goes the old nursery rhyme, ‘gunpowder, treason and plot.’ It’s a memorably succinct summary of the events of that very night in 1605, when Catholic rebel Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the Houses of Parliament and assassinate England’s Protestant king, James I. The monarch’s survival has been marked ever since and celebrations have evolved over the centuries. Traditionally, Guy’s effigy was burned on bonfires across the land, but now fireworks are the most common means of commemorating his failed — yet infamous — explosives attempt. Whichever event you choose, snack on beloved seasonal accompaniments — such as baked potatoes or toffee apples — as the dark skies over Britain become a blaze of colour. The tradition of carrying burning, tar-coated barrels through the streets of Ottery St Mary in Devon is a centuries-old tradition. Photograph by Steve Davey Photography; Alamy 1. The official sign on the banks of the River Tone at French Weir Park in Taunton advises people not to swim. But that hasn't stopped Jo, Jenny, Sue and a second Jo from enjoying a regular dip together. "People think, oh you're swimming down by the supermarket, that can't be very nice, but it's gorgeous," Jenny Hillier says, as the women huddle round with their coats and hot drinks after a bracing October plunge. People have been swimming at the spot on the River Tone in the centre of Taunton for more than a hundred years. But it is only since 2024 that French Weir Park has been designated an official bathing site, which means from May to September the water gets tested by the Environment Agency (EA). The man, who has not been identified, landed at RAF Northolt before being transported to a specialist infectious diseases unit at the Royal Free Hospital in north London. It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths. What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult? pages.text: Broadmead Road Bridge: How a broken crossing has split a community Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live How a broken London bridge has split a community 4 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Karl Mercer London political editor, in Woodford BBC Broadmead Road Bridge has been closed to all but pedestrians, bikes and motorcycles for more than three years The deserted and slightly forlorn bus stop will give you a clue that all is not well with Broadmead Road Bridge in Woodford, north-east London. There hasn't been a bus here for more than three years - or for that matter a car, a lorry or a van. Safety concerns led to the bridge, which crosses the Central line, being closed in July 2023. Financial concerns mean it hasn't yet been fixed. The local council, Redbridge, says it can't afford the £100m it would take, so has asked the government to step in. It's put in a bid to something called the structures fund - a £1bn pot of money the Department for Transport (DfT) has for infrastructure schemes that authorities across the country can apply for. It's due to announce who will be awarded funds soon. pages.description: The Thera volcano, on modern-day Santorini, buried Akrotiri in ash in the 17th or 16th century B.C.E. The eruption was one of the largest in recorded history
pages.text: Bronze Age Akrotiri Is Greek's Pompeii Skip to main content History | November 3, 2026 Greece Has Its Own Pompeii, and the Ruins Tell a Captivating Story of a Sophisticated, Seafaring Bronze Age Society The Thera volcano, on modern-day Santorini, buried Akrotiri in ash in the 17th or 16th century B.C.E. The eruption was one of the largest in recorded history The ruins of Akrotiri, a Bronze Age settlement on what is now the Greek island of Santorini Westend61 via Getty Images The ruins of Akrotiri, a Bronze Age settlement on what is now the Greek island of Santorini Westend61 via Getty Images The earth rumbled for days. Inhabitants of the seafaring Bronze Age settlement of Akrotiri watched smoke plume from Thera , a long-dormant volcano on what is now the Greek island of Santorini . People gathered their belongings and safely stored the valuables they were forced to leave behind. Then they fled by boat to nearby islands. When these minor earthquakes and eruptions subsided, residents returned to Akrotiri, collecting materials for reconstruction and beginning the arduous process of repairing the damage . But the ground continued to tremble. As conditions worsened , they made the difficult decision to flee once more, hopeful that their homes would survive the coming devastation. When Thera erupted again, the explosion was so powerful that it destroyed Akrotiri, burying the settlement (and the island that shared the volcano’s name) in some 200 feet of ash and pumice stone. Brìghde Chaimbeul: Tiny Desk Concert October 23, 2026 5:00 AM ET Lars Gotrich Credit: Photo: Vanessa Castilllo/NPR A folk revival only goes so far as an artist's understanding — and adaptation — of tradition. What themes and melodies spoke to the past can easily echo into the present, but come alive through the personality of its interpreter. Brìghde Chaimbeul expands the language of the Scottish smallpipes behind the Desk with a quiet, yet demonstrative presence. Chaimbeul grew up on the Isle of Skye, Scotland, speaking Gaelic and learning the Highland pipes before falling in love with the bellows-blown bagpipe she plays today. Drones are forever with this instrument, but Chaimbeul amplifies, manipulates and darkens the harmonics and frequencies of these pipe drones with effects pedals and contact mics that capture her percussive tapping on the chanter. The effect is mystic and ancient … completely transfixing. Sponsor Message The rhythm of language permeates the songs chosen here — deeply knitting untranslatable wordplay into the drones and melodies. BSW Degree: Your Guide to the Bachelor of Social Work Written by Coursera Staff • Updated on Jun 10, 2026 Earning your BSW is an important step if you'd like to pursue a career in social work. Key takeaways A Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) is an undergraduate degree that gives you a broad understanding of the field of social work. A BSW takes about four years and 120 credits to complete, with at least half of those credits in your social work major. Your BSW program may include coursework in human behavior, diversity or multicultural social work, social work policy and research methods, and child welfare. You can choose your BSW program based on your long-term career goals, the program’s accreditation, and field internship opportunities. Learn more about the BSW degree, including how long it takes to earn, the courses you’ll most likely take, and the paths you can follow after graduation. May 15, 2024 Español Buffet Table Tips for People with Diabetes What to know Barbecues, potlucks, holiday parties, and family reunions are gatherings to enjoy and treasure. But if you have diabetes, these events can pose special challenges to your meal plan. By using these buffet tips and choosing food wisely, you can still have a delicious meal, feel good, and have some fun! General tips Plan which foods you want to limit before you go. Also, think about which foods will help you manage your blood sugar. Check all the options on the buffet before you serve yourself. Then choose one or two favorite treats along with healthier items to round out your meal. Watch your portions. Take small servings of fatty, sugary, or salty foods like bacon, pork, desserts, or deep-fried foods. Come prepared. If possible, bring a low-fat main dish so you and others will have something healthy to eat. Focus on family and friends instead of the food. When uranium mining and milling operations, nuclear facilities, or industrial processes generate radioactive waste, safely storing those materials for up to a thousand years is a massive challenge. One solution is to build an engineered disposal cell to contain the waste. The Office of Legacy Management conducts long-term stewardship and maintenance at a number of these cells that contain low-level radioactive waste under the Uranium Mill Tailings Radiation Control Act (UMTRCA). Satellite imagery, GIS, GPS, and drones all provide the ability to gather information about the scene. However, when a disaster happens indoors, none of those capabilities carry over. The available data becomes 2D, typically a blueprint if it exists, and does not include standpipes, shutoffs, alarm panels, or AEDs. These missing elements are necessary for a safe and timely response by first responders. Without indoor spatial intelligence, responders must make high stakes and high-risk decisions with incomplete information. To address this vulnerability, NIST is actively developing best practices, design recommendations, and guidelines for utilizing building retrofit systems to improve the performance of existing structures. A whopping 27 percent of burials in and around Cambridge, England, during the 14th and 15th centuries showed skeletal evidence of bunions, compared with just 6 percent in earlier centuries. The tool can be accessed at https://bds.explorer.ces.census.gov . All tabulations in BDS Explorer are sourced from the Census API's BDS endpoint . BDS Explorer provides access to the entire BDS dataset via line charts, bar charts, and thematic maps. The application's intuitive dashboard allows for the construction of tables and charts to compare and rank measures of business dynamism such as employment, job creation and destruction, and firm births and deaths across a wide range of establishment and firm characteristics. Potential analyses include a longitudinal look at job creation by establishment age across counties, ranking establishment entry rates of young firms across NAICS industry groups and comparing job destruction rates by firm sizes across a selection of Metropolitan Areas. pages.text: Business Dynamics Statistics of Coastal Counties (BDS-CC) Business Dynamics Statistics of Coastal Counties (BDS-CC) Skip Navigation Business Dynamics Statistics of Coastal Counties (BDS-CC) January 2025 The Business Dynamics Statistics of Coastal Counties (BDS-CC) is an experimental data product extending the set of statistics published by the Business Dynamics Statistics program. The BDS-CC provides annual measures of job creation, job destruction, openings, and closings for businesses in Coastal Shoreline (CS), Coastal Non-Shoreline (CNS), and Non-Coastal (NC) counties. Counties are grouped into these categories based on definitions from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). This product allows for comparisons across industries and coastal regions of the impact of natural disasters and other events that affect coastal areas.
